title: Looking for the Best Le Labo Santal 33 Dupe? Try These Instead
summary: Looking for the best Santal 33 dupe? A Scentbird writer tested Book, Sandalwood Musk, Santal Gray, and more against the sandalwood icon.
body_markdown:
In my almost 13 years as a Scentbird writer, I’ve tried to count the exact number of times I’ve publicly declared my love for musk. However, I’ve written so many blog posts that finding the exact number would require an archaeological dig through the Scentbird archives, so let’s just agree on this: **a lot** .


Musk has always been *my note* . Clean musk, skin musk, warm musk, barely-there musk—I’m extremely easy to please when musk is involved. Until sandalwood made itself comfortable on my pulse points.


And now, the situation is clear: musk has serious competition.


There’s something almost mysterious about[sandalwood](https://www.scentbird.com/blog/sandalwood-a-sweet-and-spiritual-scent-to-wear-when-you-want-to-see-god/) . As my former dear colleague Steve put it,[Sandalwood is the Sweet and Spiritual Note To Wear When You Want to See God](https://www.scentbird.com/blog/sandalwood-a-sweet-and-spiritual-scent-to-wear-when-you-want-to-see-god/) . It can smell creamy without becoming sweet, woody without feeling heavy, and warm without announcing itself from three rooms away. Speaking of heavenly, yes, I love Le Labo Santal 33. Of course I do. That dry, papery combination of sandalwood, cedar, leather, cardamom, iris, violet, and musk has become practically its own fragrance genre. Which also explains why Santal 33 dupe searches have taken on a life of their own.


But here’s where I become difficult. As much as I love my designer fragrances and famous cult scents, every chance I get, I want to wear something a little less expected. Something distinctive enough that someone eventually leans over and asks: *I need the name of your perfume, stat.*


So instead of giving you a list of fragrances pretending to be Santal 33, I went looking through Scentbird’s sandalwood shelf for scents that scratch that same woody, dry, musky, spicy itch, and then go somewhere interesting with it. Some come remarkably close. Some take one piece of the Santal 33 formula and run away with it. Others simply understand why sandalwood people are sandalwood people.


So if you arrived here searching for a Santal 33 dupe, excellent. Stay right where you are. Just prepare to keep your Scentbird PDP links handy, because these are the fragrances that make people ask questions.


And remember: these aren’t Santal 33 copies or **** Santal 33 dupes. They’re what you wear when you’re in love with sandalwood but definitely ready to stop smelling like everyone else.


## The Best Santal 33 Dupe Options (If You Want the Closest Match)


### [Commodity – Book- Personal](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/commodity-book-personal-2309)


**Notes: cedar, rosewood, eucalyptus, bergamot, cypress, amber, musk, sandalwood**


If your primary objective is finding something that gets genuinely close to the Santal 33 experience, start here.


Commodity Book – Personal has that immediately familiar dry woods-and-skin quality, built around cedar, sandalwood, amber, and musk. There’s eucalyptus and bergamot up top, giving the woods some breathing room, while rosewood and cypress keep everything crisp rather than creamy.


Book – Personal never lets sandalwood get too creamy or sweet. Cedar keeps things dry, eucalyptus cuts through with a little freshness, and musk is there doing what musk does best: making the whole thing smell even better once it’s been on your skin for a while.


It smells like bookshelves, rainy days in Edinburgh, and everything you file under cozy yet polished.


If you typed Santal 33 dupe into Google because what you really want is that dry, woody, musky effect rather than an exact note-for-note impersonation, Book – Personal should be very high on your list.


**Santal 33 connection:** Very high. Same dry cedar-sandalwood-musk territory, with its own fresher, greener opening.


### [Experimental Perfume Club – Sandalwood Musk](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/experimental-perfume-club-sandalwood-musk-3907)


**Notes: sandalwood, pink peppercorn, vetiver, leather, ambroxan**


The name gives you Sandalwood Musk, but the fragrance has considerably more going on. Pink pepper brings the heat first, followed by smoky vetiver, sandalwood, and that smooth combination of leather and ambroxan that feels especially good once it warms up on skin.


Sandalwood Musk hits several of the elements that make Santal 33 so addictive: the dry woods, the leathery texture, and, most importantly for my fellow musk obsessives, that ambroxan-driven, almost skin-like finish.


What I especially like here is that the sandalwood doesn’t have to do all the work. Leather gives it a soft suede-like feel, while vetiver keeps things smoky and a little earthy, and ambroxan pulls the whole fragrance closer to skin. The pink pepper is more noticeable at first, then settles down and lets the warmer notes have their moment.


**Santal 33 connection:** High. Especially strong if leather, ambroxan, and dry sandalwood are what you love most about Santal 33.


### [Lake & Skye – Santal Gray](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/lake-skye-santal-gray-1636326853192)


**Notes: sandalwood, violet leaf, musk, cardamom**


Santal Gray takes several of Santal 33’s most recognizable ideas—sandalwood, violet, cardamom, musk—and strips them down into something beautifully streamlined.


It opens with cardamom, but what makes Santal Gray interesting is how quickly that spice starts rubbing shoulders with violet leaf. Suddenly the sandalwood feels cooler, almost airy, rather than dense or overly creamy. Musk comes through as it wears and gives the whole thing that close-to-skin quality that makes you keep checking your wrist.


And sandalwood sits right in the middle of it all, being sandalwood: calm, creamy, and eau so good.


There’s a reason this one sits so high on my list of Santal 33 alternatives: it has enough familiar markers to scratch the itch without making you wonder why you didn’t just wear Santal 33.


**Santal 33 connection:** High. One of the clearest choices for anyone drawn specifically to Santal 33’s cardamom-violet-musk side.


### [Scents of Wood – Sandalwood in Oak](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/scents-of-wood-sandalwood-in-oak-1674)


**Notes: sage, guaiacwood, sandalwood, oak-aged alcohol, burnt sugar**


Now we start wandering away from **Santal 33 dupe** territory, with sandalwood fragrances that want to play with your senses.


Sandalwood in Oak takes sandalwood somewhere darker, smokier, and considerably more textured. Guaiacwood and sandalwood give you the wood-on-wood situation you came for, while sage adds aromatic dryness and burnt sugar sneaks in just enough sweetness to stop the whole composition from becoming austere.


The oak-aged alcohol adds another layer of woody depth, making this feel less like polished sandalwood and more like sandalwood with some stories.


Santal 33 fans will recognize the dry woody backbone, but Sandalwood in Oak has more smoke and warmth and less of that musky skin effect.


Think related, not identical.


**Santal 33 connection:** Medium-high. Go here for the dry woods; stay for the smoky oak.


### [Scents of Wood x Scentbird Strength in Santal](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/scents-of-wood-strength-in-santal-3260)


**Notes: sandalwood, cardamom, musk, amber, aquatic notes**


You had me at sandalwood and cardamom.


Strength in Santal starts with two elements Santal 33 lovers already know very well, then changes direction with musk, amber, and an unexpected aquatic touch.


That aquatic note is where things get interesting. Instead of making sandalwood feel heavier, Strength in Santal gives it some air, almost as though you’ve taken the warm woods of Santal 33 and opened every window. Amber keeps it warm underneath, while cardamom and musk make sure sandalwood still gets plenty of attention.


The drydown smells more open and approachable without losing the sandalwood character.


**Santal 33 connection:** Medium. The cardamom-sandalwood connection is obvious, but amber and aquatic facets give this its own fresher personality.


### [Atelier Materi – Santal Blond](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/atelier-materi-santal-blond-4334)


**Notes: sandalwood, cardamom, jasmine, tonka bean**


Santal Blond proves exactly why I don’t want this list to be nothing but literal Santal 33 dupes.


Because look what happens when you take sandalwood and cardamom—the combination we already know works spectacularly—and introduce jasmine and tonka bean.


Everything gets softer, rounder, and a little more sensual. The sandalwood still gives the fragrance its woody backbone and cardamom keeps some aromatic spice running through it, but jasmine adds floral brightness while tonka brings warmth and gentle sweetness.


This is less papery sandalwood, more cashmere sandalwood.


And that’s exactly why it belongs here. It gives you enough of the sandalwood-cardamom pairing to feel familiar, then jasmine and tonka take it somewhere softer and more sensual.


**Santal 33 connection:** Medium. Familiar sandalwood-cardamom DNA with a warmer, smoother, more floral direction.


### [Fragrance Du Bois – Santal Complet](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/fragrance-du-bois-santal-complet-69111441863313)


**Notes: sandalwood, lemon, creamy and resinous notes**


If Santal 33 gives you sandalwood with edges, Santal Complet starts sanding them down.


Here, sandalwood is creamy, rich, and enveloping, brightened by lemon before settling into a smoother, more resinous warmth.


This is where sandalwood gets to show off its softer side. And if you’ve only fallen for the note through dry, minimalist fragrances, Santal Complet is a very good reminder that sandalwood contains multitudes. It doesn’t have to smell papery or leathery to be compelling. Sometimes it can simply be plush.


Very plush. Take-your-shoes-off-the-carpet-is-expensive plush.


**Santal 33 connection:** Medium. Less leather, less dryness, more creaminess—but still centered on the note that brought us all here.


### [Sana Jardin – Sandalwood Temple](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/sana-jardin-sandalwood-temple-3269)


**Notes: sandalwood, neroli, cedar, vetiver**


Sandalwood Temple is what I’d point you toward if you love sandalwood but want to take some of the sharpness out of it. Neroli brings brightness before cedar, sandalwood, and vetiver start warming things up, giving you a version of sandalwood that feels greener and easier rather than particularly dark or dense.


Compared with Santal 33, it’s greener and brighter, without as much leather or musky warmth. But if the thing you love about Santal 33 is how woods can somehow feel both calming and incredibly cool, Sandalwood Temple absolutely understands the ask.


**Santal 33 connection:** Medium-low. Less of a smell-alike, more of a compelling alternative for someone who wants their sandalwood fresher and greener.


### [Heretic Parfum – Scandalwood](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/heretic-parfums-scandalwood-3125)


**Notes: cedar, coriander, Bulgarian rose, sandalwood, labdanum, musk**


First of all: Scandalwood. Respect to whoever thought of the name.


Second: this is what a scent smells like when sandalwood (or the Heretic founder, more likely) decides minimalism has had enough attention.


Cedar and sandalwood establish the woody foundation, but coriander brings spice, Bulgarian rose adds floral richness, labdanum turns up the warmth, and musk, like the Cancer sign of the zodiac pulls everyone together on skin.


It’s rosier and more resinous than Santal 33, which is precisely why I’d recommend it to someone who already owns, or has smelled, a million fragrances trying to recreate Santal 33.


Scandalwood takes the recognizable sandalwood-and-musk pairing and piles on rose, coriander, and labdanum, so there’s considerably more warmth and richness happening here. In other words, this is where our search for a Santal 33 dupe starts getting a little scandalous.


Sorry. The name practically wrote that one for me.


**Santal 33 connection:** Low-medium. The shared woody-musky foundation is there, but Scandalwood takes it in a warmer, rosier direction.


### [Memoire Archives – Cabin Retreat](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/memoire-archives-cabin-retreat-1765)


**Notes: cedarwood, oakmoss, sandalwood**


If Santal 33 makes you think *wood* , Cabin Retreat says, “Fine. Let’s commit.”


Cedarwood and sandalwood create a dry woody foundation while oakmoss brings in an earthy, green character that pushes the fragrance toward the forest rather than the skin.


Cabin Retreat is also refreshingly straightforward about what it came here to do. Cedarwood and sandalwood dominate, while oakmoss gives all that wood a damp, green edge. If Santal 33 is the smell of beautifully finished wood, Cabin Retreat gets you a little closer to the tree.


Compared with Santal 33, it loses much of the leather-and-musk effect and goes greener instead. But for anyone whose favorite part of Santal 33 is its woody dryness, Cabin Retreat offers a very appealing detour.


Also, possibly the cheapest imaginary cabin you’ll ever acquire.


**Santal 33 connection:** Low-medium. More mossy woods than musky woods, but the dry sandalwood appeal remains.


### [Maison 21G Sleek – Sandalwood](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/maison-21g-sleek-sandalwood-3531)


**Notes: sandalwood, sesame absolute, cypriol**


And now for the wildcard.


Sleek Sandalwood takes the note somewhere earthier and spicier with sesame absolute and cypriol, creating a profile that feels nuttier, darker, and more unusual than the classic Santal 33 blueprint.


This isn’t the fragrance I’d hand someone demanding the closest possible match. It *is* the fragrance I’d hand someone who said, “I love Santal 33. Show me something I probably haven’t smelled five times already.”


Sesame gives the sandalwood an intriguing toasted quality while cypriol reinforces the dry, earthy woods. The result feels familiar enough to satisfy the sandalwood craving and unusual enough to warrant the inevitable second sniff, which, frankly, is exactly what I want from perfume.


**Santal 33 connection:** Low-medium. Same sandalwood obsession, completely different extracurricular activities.


## **So, What’s the Best Santal 33 Alternative?**


If you’re specifically looking for a Santal 33 dupe, Commodity Book – Personal, Experimental Perfume Club Sandalwood Musk, and Lake & Skye Santal Gray come closest to the dry, woody, musky, spicy territory that made the original such a phenomenon.


But I’m going to make a case for not stopping there.


Sandalwood is far too interesting a note to spend all its time impersonating one fragrance. Wear it smoky, creamy, green, spicy, musky, rosy, resinous, or strange enough that you keep smelling your own wrist at your desk and completely lose track of what you were doing.


Because the best Santal 33 dupe isn’t actually a dupe; it’s rather the fragrance that makes you forget you were looking for Santal 33 in the first place.
